actor_namespaces.key_format: service name, e.g. fixture-loader, import-worker, connector.<name>

categories.description: Deployed runtime unit: container workload, web app, function, service process
Virtual machine, instance or physical host
An API published on a gateway or platform
Database server or instance hosting databases
Database, bucket, file share or cache holding data

entity_types.description: Organization-defined environment; its name and key are the organization's
Kubernetes namespace on any provider's cluster; provider = its cluster's provider
Provider account or hierarchy node (ADR-0019 §4); nesting per provider scope rules
Fallback for any provider (E04); parent only where the provider's native hierarchy shows it

identity_namespaces.uniqueness_scope: embedded project, folder or organization path

identity_namespaces.format: stable key from a registered source (CMDB, private-cloud platform, custom technology, import file)

relationship_types.description: Hierarchical containment (composition): child is part of exactly one parent; resource or logical family, never mixed; physical within one provider
Logical membership (grouping), many-to-many; acyclic by construction
Stewardship: team owns an entity (INV-05, many-to-many)
Consumer of a channel (receiving from a queue counts)
Reads from a data store; edge points actor to store (dependency direction)
Writes to a data store; edge points actor to store (dependency direction)
Uses a data store; access direction not established by the evidence; never converted automatically
Explicitly configured infrastructure connectivity; never inferred from traffic
Curated dependency between logical things; never produced by connectors, imports of other types or inference
Security control protects resource; no control types in v1
Design rationale link to an ADR (Phase 3)

automatic: infra.* -> provider-specific type of the same provider whose fixed native_type equals the entity's native_type
infra.resource -> the neutral type of the category that the entity's taxonomy version maps its native_type to

versioning.identity_rule: entity and relationship IDs never change across taxonomy versions; every version row records the taxonomy version it was validated against
versioning.major: removes or renames anything, narrows a rule, or makes an attribute required; needs a data migration plan and owner approval
versioning.minor: adds types, relationship types, pairs, enumeration values, optional attributes, providers, namespaces, mappings
